notes: Medicaid and other state-sponsored programs serve low-income people and people with disabilities and are a large business. No Medicaid-specific membership or revenue figure appears in the provided text. The 32% figure covers all U.S. government agencies (Medicare, FEP and others), so level 4 customer access was not assigned; when torn, the lower level was chosen. Several items were not scored as Community investment: the social determinants of health program, the Food as Medicine strategy and work with community organizations. They are member health services or general statements with no grants, dollars or participant numbers. Patient education in care management falls under the 'educating customers' trap. Workforce demographics are referred to the annual Impact Report and were not scored. The values statement and the 'committed to ensuring that all people... can receive individualized care' language is a claim only. The executive title changed from 'Chief Talent & Diversity Officer' to 'Chief Talent Officer', but practices disclosed (BRGs, pay equity) are scored regardless of label. Traps ignored: 'joint venture' (Mosaic Health), 'foundation of our strategy', 'community engagement requirements' (OBBBA Medicaid rules), 'Student Health' (customer type, not education), 'diversified mix' and 'diversification'. Medicare Part D exit in 2026 is planned and does not affect scores.
